files.purpose: SwiftUI drawer that renders the per-thread terminal panel: a 38pt tab strip of TerminalTab chips with a plus button and a hide chevron, the hosted SwiftTerm view (TerminalHost/TerminalHostContainer), an AppKit drag handle on its top edge (TerminalResizeHandle/TerminalResizeHandleView) that resizes the drawer, and an empty state shown when every tab is closed.

feature_notes: The drawer is resized from a dedicated 8pt strip overlaid on the band above the tabs, deliberately not the whole tab row, so a sideways drag across the tabs scrolls them instead of moving the drawer
Height is clamped with min(760, max(140, origin + delta)); the drag writes only @State, and settings (hence user defaults) are written once on mouseUp
mouseUp applies one final onChange with the release delta before calling onEnd, so the release position counts
The grip bar appears only on hover or while dragging, widening from 12 to 28 over 0.18 s easeOut and fading 0 to 0.6 opacity
The strip installs a resizeUpDown cursor rect so the pointer shows the affordance before any press; acceptsFirstMouse is true so an inactive window resizes on the first click

Escape in the terminal closes the panel only when the shell itself owns the terminal foreground, no allowed modifiers are held, and the terminal view is the window's first responder; a foreground program (vim, claude, less) still receives Escape. When it acts, the monitor swallows the event by returning nil

A newly opened terminal takes keyboard focus once when runtime.terminalWantsFocus is set; the focus move happens in a main-actor Task rather than during the SwiftUI update, and the flag is cleared first
Appearance is re-applied on every updateNSView via session.applyAppearance(isDark:), which itself no-ops unless the value changed

During a window live resize the hosted terminal's autoresizingMask is parked to [] and its frame is synced at most once per 50 ms beat, then restored to [.width, .height] and synced once more at didEndLiveResize, so SwiftTerm re-wraps far less often
syncFrame is a no-op unless the hosted view is still this container's subview, bounds width and height are greater than 0, and the frame actually differs

The panel calls ensureTerminal on appear, so opening the drawer in a thread with no shells spawns one; if the reader closes every tab the drawer stays open showing the empty state with its "New shell" button
The hosted terminal is keyed by .id(selected.id), so switching tabs swaps the hosted NSView rather than mutating one representable
unresolved_questions: Chrome.sheetCornerRadius, Chrome.iconFont, Chrome.secondaryText and the .chip and .glass button styles are defined outside this bundle, so their literal values are not captured here
ShortcutStore.hint(for: .toggleTerminal) formatting, the exact appended hint text, is defined elsewhere
KeyChord.allowedModifiers membership is defined elsewhere, so which modifier combinations still let Escape close the panel is not pinned down
session.view.process.shellPid comes from SwiftTerm's LocalProcess, outside this repository's sources

files.purpose: Owns the app's live shells: TerminalSession wraps one SwiftTerm LocalProcessTerminalView running a login shell in a pseudo terminal with Droppy-specific environment, TerminalBridge receives SwiftTerm's process callbacks, and TerminalStore keeps per-thread arrays of sessions plus the selected tab with open, run, ensure, restart, close, closeAll and terminateAll.

Light colours: background NSColor(white: 0.985, alpha: 1), foreground NSColor(white: 0.12, alpha: 1)
Caret colour = Chrome.accentNSColor; selection background = Chrome.accentNSColor.withAlphaComponent(0.3)
feature_notes: Each session starts the user's login shell from LoginEnvironment.userShell() with argv[0] set to "-<shellname>" so profile files run

Environment overrides on top of LoginEnvironment.current: TERM=xterm-256color, COLORTERM=truecolor, TERM_PROGRAM=Droppy Code, DROPPY_CODE_PROJECT_ROOT=<project directory>; the dictionary is flattened to "KEY=VALUE" strings for startProcess

With a command the arguments are exactly ["-l", "-i", "-c", "<command>; exec <shell> -l"], so the script runs and the tab then becomes an interactive login shell instead of exiting; with no command the argument array is empty
selected(for:) returns the session whose id matches selection[threadID], falling back to the LAST session in the thread, so a stale selection still shows a tab
open(...) appends the new session to the thread's array and immediately makes it the selection, returning it (@discardableResult)
run(_ script:threadID:directory:) is open(...) with script.name as the title and script.command as the startup command
ensureTerminal(threadID:directory:) opens a shell only when the thread has none

restart(_:) terminates the old shell and substitutes a fresh session at the same index in the row, keeping the title and directory and dropping any startup command (command: nil), then selects the fresh one; if the old session is no longer in the array the fresh one is appended
close(_:) terminates and removes the session, and if it was the selected one the selection falls back to the last remaining session's id, or nil when none remain
closeAll(for:) terminates every session of the thread and sets both sessions[threadID] and selection[threadID] to nil
terminateAll() terminates every session across every thread without clearing the dictionaries, an app-shutdown sweep
terminate() is idempotent: it returns early unless isRunning is true

The SwiftTerm delegate callbacks sizeChanged, setTerminalTitle and hostCurrentDirectoryUpdate are deliberately empty bodies, so the tab title never follows the shell's OSC title or its current directory; only processTerminated does anything
foregroundJobIsTheShell returns false for a non-positive pid or a failed sysctl, and otherwise true only when the terminal foreground process group equals the shell's own process group
